olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Prove that for each positive integer $n$, there are pairwise relatively prime integers $k_0,k_1,\ldots,k_n>1$ such that $k_0k_1\cdots k_n-1$ is the product of two consecutive integers.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute scalene $\triangle ABC$; $M,N,P$ = midpoints of $BC,CA,AB$. Perpendicular bisectors of $AB,AC$ meet ray $AM$ at $D,E$; lines $BD,CE$ meet at $F$ inside $\triangle ABC$. Prove $A,N,F,P$ lie on one circle.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $S_n=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|x|+|y+\frac{1}{2}|<n\}$. A path is a sequence of distinct adjacent lattice points in $S_n$. Prove $S_n$ cannot be partitioned into fewer than $n$ paths.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A regular $n$-gon ($n\geq 3$) has a triangulation into $n-2$ triangles using $n-3$ non-crossing diagonals. If all triangles are isosceles, find all possible $n$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Three nonneg­ative reals $r_1,r_2,r_3$ with $a_1r_1+a_2r_2+a_3r_3=0$ for some not-all-zero integers $a_i$. Permitted: choose $x\leq y$ on board, erase $y$, write $y-x$. Prove after finitely many such operations, at least one 0 appears.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2008

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: At a conference, every pair of mathematicians are friends or strangers. Each eats in one of two rooms, wanting a room with an even number of friends. Prove the number of valid room-splits is a power of 2.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 2008
